newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's TrizecHahn seeks Hollywood project.
newsitem.headline: Canada's TrizecHahn seeks Hollywood project.

text.p: Toronto-based TrizecHahn Corp. is seeking to redevelop part of world famous Hollywood Boulevard and Mann's Chinese Theater with a $150 million retail and entertainment complex.

TrizecHahn, one of North America's largest publicly traded real estate developers, said this week that officials of the Los Angeles Community Redevelopment Board recommended to the agency that it negotiate exclusively with TrizecHahn to redevelop the well-known site.

"It doesn't necessarily mean that at the end of the day we're going to do the deal. We are very confident and optimistic, but there are business terms to be worked out and there's still a negotiating process," Laurie Ludwick, director of media relations for TrizecHahn, told Reuters.

The agency had sought proposals to redevelop the site, located at Hollywood Boulevard and Highland Avenue and best known for Hollywood's Walk of Fame. The agency wants to revitalize the area, similar to the redevelopment of Times Square in New York. The area attracted about 5 million tourists in 1996
The TrizecHahn proposal involves a 425,000-square-foot retail and entertainment complex.
Anchoring the development would be a 13-screen, 5,000 seat multiplex operated by CinAmerica, a joint venture of Viacom Inc.s Paramount Communications Inc., and Time Warner Inc.
The proposal includes expanding Mann's Chinese Theater and building another theater known as the Babylon, which film studios would use for film premieres.
TrizecHahn hopes to have all major Hollywood studios represented in the complex, with studio stores selling movie-related merchandise.

The company said the Community Redevelopment Board would likely decide within the next 30 days whether to deal exclusively with it. Ludwick said that if TrizecHahn's proposal was accepted, about six months of negotiations would follow.
Assuming approval of TrizecHahn's proposal, construction is expected to begin in 1998, with completion targeted for the year 2000.
